surface: REST/HTML form (Spring Boot z/OS Connect Customer Services and Payment interfaces)
auth_model: None in the runnable code: the Spring Boot interfaces have no Spring Security and accept anonymous requests; the Liberty JAX-RS web.xml declares no security constraints and disables XSRF protection; the checked-in z/OS Connect server.xml defines a basicRegistry (ibmuser/SYS1) but sets requireAuth=false and requireSecure=false. Any enforcement would have to come from CICS/Liberty SAF configuration outside this repo (needs confirmation).

findings.title: No machine-readable API spec for the Liberty JAX-RS JSON API or the Spring Boot interfaces; Swagger 2.0 exists only for the 10 z/OS Connect APIs
findings.evidence: `ls src/zosconnect_artefacts/apis/` lists exactly 10 API projects (creacc, crecust, delacc, delcus, inqacccz, inqaccz, inqcustz, makepayment, updacc, updcust), each with a Swagger 2.0 `api-docs/swagger.json`. No OpenAPI/Swagger document, `@Operation`/`@OpenAPIDefinition` annotation, or springdoc/MicroProfile OpenAPI dependency exists for the 34 JAX-RS routes under `src/webui/src/main/java/com/ibm/cics/cip/bankliberty/api/json/` (class roots `/account`, `/customer`, `/counter`, `/processedTransaction`, `/companyName`, `/sortCode`) or the 21 Spring MVC routes in the two z/OS Connect interface modules (`find . -iname '*openapi*' -o -iname 'swagger*'` returns only the zosconnect_artefacts files). Route-vs-spec diff: the JAX-RS API is therefore 100% unspecified; the 10 z/OS Connect specs match the service archives in `src/zosconnect_artefacts/services/` one-to-one.
findings.remediation: Generate and commit an OpenAPI 3 document for the Liberty JSON API with MicroProfile OpenAPI annotations (Liberty `mpOpenAPI` feature) and for the Spring modules with springdoc-openapi; lint all specs with Spectral in CI and fail the build when mounted routes and spec paths diverge (e.g. springdoc + `openapi-diff` in a contract-test stage).

findings.title: Money-moving POST/PUT endpoints have no idempotency mechanism
findings.evidence: `grep -rni idempot src --include=*.java` returns no matches. `POST /paymentinterface-1.1/submit` and `POST /paymentinterface-1.1/paydbcr` forward a PAYDBCR debit/credit to z/OS Connect `PUT /makepayment/dbcr` (COBOL DBCRFUN) and the JAX-RS `PUT /account/debit/{id}`, `/account/credit/{id}` and `/account/transfer/{id}` (AccountsResource lines 790, 856, 923) apply balance changes directly; none reads an `Idempotency-Key` header or any client request id. Runtime: repeated anonymous `curl -s -i -X POST 'http://localhost:19080/paymentinterface-1.1/submit?acctnum=12345678&amount=10.50&organisation=ACME'` requests were each accepted with HTTP 200 and each produced a new outbound backend attempt in the log; no header is required to distinguish retries from new payments.
findings.remediation: Require an `Idempotency-Key` header on every money-moving POST/PUT, persist key + request hash + response in a keyed store (Db2 table or Redis) and replay the stored response on duplicates; propagate the key to the z/OS Connect/CICS call as the PROCTRAN reference so retries are detectable end to end.

findings.title: API version is hard-coded in the servlet context path and bumped in bulk commits; JAX-RS routes are unversioned
findings.evidence: `server.servlet.context-path=/paymentinterface-1.1` and `/customerservices-1.0` are the only versioning mechanism; the Liberty JAX-RS paths (`/account`, `/customer`, ...) carry no version. `git log -S"paymentinterface-1.1" -- src/Z-OS-Connect-Payment-Interface` shows the 1.0 to 1.1 bump landed in commit 840b982 (2024-07-23, "Update to source") with no changelog or deprecation note. The deployment guide (etc/install/springBootUI/doc) requires editing `ConnectionInfo.java` source to change the backend host/port.
findings.remediation: Adopt URI-path versioning (`/api/v1/...`) for the JAX-RS and Spring APIs, document a deprecation policy (Sunset/Deprecation headers) and record route changes in a CHANGELOG; externalise host/port with Spring `@ConfigurationProperties` instead of source edits.

findings.title: Spring Boot Payment and Customer Services interfaces expose state-changing routes with no authentication
findings.evidence: Neither module declares Spring Security (no `spring-boot-starter-security` in either pom.xml, no `SecurityFilterChain`, no `@PreAuthorize`). Runtime transcript: `curl -s -i -X POST 'http://localhost:19080/paymentinterface-1.1/submit?acctnum=12345678&amount=10.50&organisation=ACME'` returned `HTTP/1.1 200` (empty body, see CBSA-D-01) without any credential; `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST http://localhost:19081/customerservices-1.0/delcust --data-urlencode 'custNumber=1'` and `/createcust`, `/updateacc` likewise returned 200 anonymously and attempted the backend call. Actual ledger mutation could not be confirmed because the z/OS Connect backend host `winmvsb0.hursley.ibm.com` does not resolve from the VM.
findings.remediation: Add Spring Security with OAuth 2.0 resource-server JWT validation (or mTLS for service clients), deny-all by default, and require a dedicated scope/role for payment and customer-mutation routes; pass the caller identity to z/OS Connect instead of a shared server credential.

findings.title: Liberty JAX-RS JSON API declares no security constraints, disables XSRF protection, and authorises nothing at object level
findings.evidence: web.xml contains only `disable-xsrf-protection=true` and `syncId=false`; there is no `<security-constraint>`, `<login-config>` or `<security-role>`, no `@RolesAllowed`/`@DenyAll` and no `SecurityContext` use anywhere under `src/webui/src/main/java/com/ibm/cics/cip/bankliberty/api/json/` (grep returns nothing). All 34 routes, including `PUT /account/debit/{id}`, `PUT /account/credit/{id}`, `PUT /account/transfer/{id}`, `DELETE /account/{accountNumber}`, `DELETE /customer/{id}`, `POST/DELETE /counter/*` and the six `POST /processedTransaction/*` audit-record writers, select the target purely from the path/body identifier. Code-level only: the WAR cannot run on the VM (needs CICS, Db2, VSAM); whether the CICS Liberty JVM server enforces SAF `appSecurity` in front of it is listed under needs_confirmation.
findings.remediation: Enable Liberty `appSecurity-5.0` with SAF/LDAP registry and `<security-constraint>` per route group, annotate resources with `@RolesAllowed`, and implement object-level checks (caller may only act on accounts owned by their customer id) in a shared filter; move `/processedTransaction` and `/counter` writers behind an internal-only role.

findings.title: Payment API binds amounts as float and accepts unbounded or non-finite values and oversize identifiers
findings.evidence: `@RequestParam("amount") float amount` with no Bean Validation. Runtime: `curl -s -i -X POST 'http://localhost:19080/paymentinterface-1.1/submit?acctnum=123456789012345678901234567890&amount=-99999999999&organisation=AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA'` returned HTTP 200 and the log recorded `Amount -9.9999998E10` (float rounding visible). `amount=NaN` was also accepted and serialised into the outbound PAYDBCR JSON as `"COMM_AMT":"NaN"`. `TransferForm.amount` in the browser path is a boxed `Float` with no range constraint.
findings.remediation: Replace float with `BigDecimal` (or integer minor units) in a validated request DTO using Jakarta Bean Validation (`@NotNull @Digits(integer=10,fraction=2) @DecimalMin("0.01")`), bound `acctnum`/`organisation` with `@Pattern`/`@Size`, and reject non-finite input before building the z/OS Connect request.

findings.title: Bean Validation annotations are silently ignored (javax.validation on Spring Boot 3), so unvalidated identifiers are concatenated into the backend URL path
findings.evidence: `WebController` imports `javax.validation.Valid` (line 9) and `AccountEnquiryForm` declares `@NotNull @Size(max = 8)` from `javax.validation.constraints` (lines 6-16), but Spring Boot 3.3.7 only honours `jakarta.validation`; no `spring-boot-starter-validation` dependency is present. Line 152-153 builds `ConnectionInfo.getAddressAndPort() + "/inqaccz/enquiry/" + accountEnquiryForm.getAcctNumber()` by string concatenation. Runtime: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST http://localhost:19081/customerservices-1.0/enqacct --data-urlencode 'acctNumber=../../zosConnect/apis'` -> 200 and `--data-urlencode 'acctNumber=1234567890123456789012345678901234567890'` -> 200; the WebClientRequestException count in the application log rose from 5 to 7, proving both values passed validation and reached the outbound WebClient. The same pattern is used for `/delcus/remove/`, `/inqcustz/enquiry/` and `/inqacccz/list/`.
findings.remediation: Add `spring-boot-starter-validation`, migrate all constraint imports to `jakarta.validation`, use `@Pattern(regexp="\\d{1,8}")` on identifiers, and build backend URLs with `UriBuilder`/`WebClient.uri("/inqaccz/enquiry/{acc}", acc)` so path segments are encoded rather than concatenated.

findings.title: No explicit request-size policy; oversized bodies are handled only by Tomcat defaults
findings.evidence: Both application.properties files set only `server.port` and `server.servlet.context-path`. Runtime: posting a 3 MB form body to `/paymentinterface-1.1/submit` returned HTTP 400 after 1,835,008 bytes were uploaded (Tomcat's default `max-swallow-size`/parameter limits), not a configured 413.
findings.remediation: Set `server.tomcat.max-http-form-post-size`, `server.tomcat.max-swallow-size` and `spring.servlet.multipart.max-request-size` explicitly, enforce the same limit at the ingress/WAF, and return RFC 9457 `413` problem+json.

findings.title: Backend connection failure is converted into HTTP 200 with an empty body
findings.evidence: The handler catches `Exception`, logs it at INFO and `return null`. Runtime: `curl -s -i -X POST 'http://localhost:19080/paymentinterface-1.1/submit?acctnum=12345678&amount=10.50&organisation=ACME'` -> `HTTP/1.1 200`, `Content-Length: 0`; application log: `WebClientRequestException: Failed to resolve 'winmvsb0.hursley.ibm.com'`. Customer Services `WebController` uses the same pattern (catch Exception -> log -> render page with HTTP 200) for every POST route.
findings.remediation: Introduce a `@RestControllerAdvice` mapping `WebClientRequestException`/`WebClientResponseException` to 502/504 RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` responses with a correlation id, and never return null from a handler.

findings.title: Blank amount on the browser payment form produces an unhandled HTTP 500 (NullPointerException)
findings.evidence: `TransferForm.amount` is a nullable `Float`; after `@Valid` (javax, ignored) the controller calls `transferForm.getAmount().floatValue()` indirectly via `PaymentInterfaceJson`. Runtime: `curl -s -i -X POST http://localhost:19080/paymentinterface-1.1/paydbcr --data-urlencode 'acctNumber=1' --data-urlencode 'amount=' --data-urlencode 'organisation=ACME'` -> `HTTP/1.1 500` with the default Spring error envelope `{"timestamp":...,"status":500,"error":"Internal Server Error","path":"/paymentinterface-1.1/paydbcr"}`; log: `java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.lang.Float.floatValue()" because the return value of ...TransferForm.getAmount() is null`.
findings.remediation: Fix validation activation (see CBSA-C-02), check `BindingResult` before use, and add a global exception handler so unexpected exceptions return a stable problem-details envelope.

findings.title: Local transfer applies debit and credit as two independent updates and ignores their results; rollback only covers the audit-record write
findings.evidence: `transferLocalInternal` calls `db2Account.debitCredit(negativeAmount)` (line 1081), swaps the account number (1083) and calls `db2Account.debitCredit(amount)` (1085) without checking either boolean return value; `Task.getTask().rollback()` is invoked only when the subsequent PROCTRAN write fails (lines 1098-1107). A failed or rejected credit after a successful debit therefore leaves the debit committed at the end of the CICS unit of work. Code-level only: the Liberty WAR needs CICS/Db2 and could not be run on the VM.
findings.remediation: Check both `debitCredit` results and roll back the CICS unit of work (`Task.getTask().rollback()`) on any failure, or perform the transfer as a single SQL transaction/COBOL program (DBCRFUN-style) with an explicit balance-check-and-update; add a contract test for the debit-ok/credit-fail path.

findings.title: No correlation/request id is returned to callers or written to logs
findings.evidence: Runtime: `curl -s -i http://localhost:19080/paymentinterface-1.1/does-not-exist` returned the default envelope `{"timestamp","status":404,"error","path"}` and no `X-Request-Id`/`traceparent` header; application log lines carry thread name only (`[io-19080-exec-5]`). No Micrometer Tracing/Sleuth dependency or MDC usage exists in either module.
findings.remediation: Add `micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel` (or a servlet filter generating `X-Request-Id`), put the id in the logback pattern via MDC, and echo it in the problem+json envelope.

findings.title: Application logs contain account numbers, amounts, organisation and the full outbound payment JSON
findings.evidence: Runtime log (INFO level, default pattern): `AcctNumber: 12345678, Amount 10.5, Organisation ACME` followed by the serialised PAYDBCR object containing `COMM_ACCNO` and `COMM_AMT`. Customer Services logs `Json to be sent:` plus the full `CreateCustomerJson` including name, address and date of birth (`WebController` lines 500-520). Logging is unstructured printf-style (logback default pattern, `logger.info(obj.toString())`).
findings.remediation: Switch to structured JSON logging (logstash-logback-encoder), log a masked account reference and correlation id only, and add a log-redaction unit test; define the org data-classification list of fields that must never be logged.

findings.title: Customer Services module has no health/readiness endpoint and neither module exposes metrics
findings.evidence: Runtime: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:19081/customerservices-1.0/actuator/health` -> 404. Payment exposes `/actuator` with only `health` (`{"status":"UP"}`) via the transitively included actuator; no `prometheus`/`metrics` endpoint is enabled and `management.endpoints.*` is unset in both modules. 5xx responses are only detectable from free-text ERROR stack traces.
findings.remediation: Add `spring-boot-starter-actuator` to both modules, expose `health,info,prometheus` with liveness/readiness groups, and alert on the `http_server_requests_seconds_count{status=~"5.."}` metric.

findings.title: Checked-in z/OS Connect server.xml ships default credentials, HTTP-only endpoint, wildcard CORS with credentials, and requireAuth/requireSecure=false
findings.evidence: `<user name="ibmuser" password="SYS1" />` in a `basicRegistry` (lines 16-22), `<httpEndpoint ... httpPort="30701">` (30-43), `<cors allowedOrigins="*" allowCredentials="true" ...>` and `<zosconnect_zosConnectManager requireAuth="false" requireSecure="false" ...>` (line 75). These are the APIs that the Spring interfaces call for every customer/account/payment operation (DBCRFUN, CREACC, DELCUS, ...). Code-level: the z/OS Connect server cannot run on the VM.
findings.remediation: Remove credentials from source control (SAF registry or Liberty `<variable>` injected from a secret store), set `requireAuth="true" requireSecure="true"`, serve only HTTPS with a keystore, restrict `allowedOrigins` to the two UI hosts, and rotate `ibmuser`.

findings.title: Spring Boot 3.3.7 dependency tree carries 18 critical and 67 high OSV advisories with fixes available
findings.evidence: Resolved trees (`mvn dependency:list`) were queried against api.osv.dev (query + per-vuln severity/fix lookup). 85 HIGH/CRITICAL advisories with a fixed version across 29 artifacts, e.g. `org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core` 10.1.34 (7 critical incl. CVE-2025-24813, 12 high), `org.thymeleaf:thymeleaf` 3.1.2/3.1.3 and `thymeleaf-spring6` 3.1.3 (3 critical each, fixed 3.1.5.RELEASE), `io.netty:netty-handler` 4.1.116.Final (1 critical, fixed 4.1.137.Final), `org.springframework:spring-webmvc` 6.1.16 (1 critical CVE-2026-47884). Full table in the report appendix; `de.codecentric:spring-boot-admin-server` 3.2.3 (Payment pom line 128) pulls the extra netty-codec-* artifacts.
findings.remediation: Upgrade the parent to the current Spring Boot 3.5.x line (brings Tomcat 10.1.5x, Netty 4.1.13x, Framework 6.2.x), bump `thymeleaf` to 3.1.5.RELEASE, drop the unused `spring-boot-admin-server`, and gate CI with `osv-scanner`/Dependabot on high+critical.

findings.title: No security response headers on the Spring Boot interfaces
findings.evidence: Runtime: `curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://localhost:19080/paymentinterface-1.1/` returned only Content-Type/Content-Language/Transfer-Encoding/Date; no `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `Strict-Transport-Security`, `Referrer-Policy` or `Cache-Control`. (Positive: an `OPTIONS /submit` preflight from `Origin: https://evil.example` was rejected with 403, i.e. no permissive CORS.)
findings.remediation: Add Spring Security's headers DSL (or a `OncePerRequestFilter`) emitting nosniff, CSP, HSTS, Referrer-Policy and `Cache-Control: no-store` for API responses.

findings.title: Payment WAR bundles spring-boot-admin-server 3.2.3 that is never enabled
findings.evidence: `de.codecentric:spring-boot-admin-server` is declared at compile scope; `grep -rn EnableAdminServer src/` finds no usage, yet `unzip -l target/paymentinterface-1.1.war` contains `spring-boot-admin-server-3.2.3.jar`. It enlarges the attack surface (extra netty codecs, httpcore5 with high advisories, see CBSA-F-02) for no function.
findings.remediation: Remove the dependency; if an admin console is wanted, run it as a separate secured service with `spring-boot-admin-starter-client` only.

findings.title: No CI quality gates, contract tests, spec linting, changelog or automated deploy/rollback for the HTTP surfaces
findings.evidence: The repository has no `.github/` directory, no `Jenkinsfile`/`.gitlab-ci.yml`, no `CHANGELOG*`, and no test sources in either Spring module (`src/test` absent); the deployment guide is a manual procedure (edit `ConnectionInfo.java`, `mvn package`, copy WAR to the Liberty `apps` directory, restart the JVM server) with no rollback step. No `@Deprecated` or `Deprecation`/`Sunset` header use exists in the route classes.
findings.remediation: Add a GitHub Actions workflow running `mvn verify` with Spring MockMvc contract tests, Spectral lint of the OpenAPI documents, `osv-scanner`, and a versioned WAR artifact publish; document rollback as redeploying the previous artifact version.

positives: Both Spring Boot modules build cleanly with `mvn -q -DskipTests package` (Maven 3.6.3, JDK 17) and start without a backend, which made local probing possible.

Swagger 2.0 definitions exist for all 10 z/OS Connect APIs under `src/zosconnect_artefacts/apis/*/api-docs/swagger.json` and map one-to-one to service archives and COBOL programs (CREACC, CRECUST, DELACC, DELCUS, INQACCCU, INQACC, INQCUST, DBCRFUN, UPDACC, UPDCUST).
The Spring MVC CORS default is deny: an `OPTIONS /paymentinterface-1.1/submit` preflight from a foreign origin returned 403.

The JAX-RS transfer path validates business rules before writing: rejects same-account transfers (400), non-positive amounts (400), unknown source/target accounts (404), and calls `Task.getTask().rollback()` when the PROCTRAN audit write fails.
Db2 access in the Liberty API uses `PreparedStatement` with bound parameters for the inspected account/customer queries, limiting SQL-injection surface.
Request models in the Spring modules already carry Bean Validation annotations (`@NotNull`, `@Size`); only the javax to jakarta migration is missing to make them effective.
Default Spring error envelope does not leak stack traces (`server.error.include-stacktrace` default `never`); 404/500 bodies contain only timestamp/status/error/path.
The Payment module exposes `/actuator/health` returning `{"status":"UP"}` and the actuator index lists only `health`.
needs_confirmation: Liberty JAX-RS WAR (`src/webui`) could not be started: it needs a CICS TS region with JCICS, Db2 and VSAM; CBSA-B-02 and CBSA-D-03 are therefore code-level and the runtime behaviour (actual IDOR, debit-without-credit) is unconfirmed.
Whether the CICS Liberty JVM server configuration (not in this repo) enables `appSecurity` / SAF and adds `<security-constraint>`s in front of the JSON API.
Whether deployed z/OS Connect servers override the checked-in `etc/install/base/zosconnectserver/server.xml` (`requireAuth=false`, `ibmuser/SYS1`).
Whether the Spring Boot UIs are deployed behind an authenticating reverse proxy/WAF in any environment; the repo and deployment guide do not mention one.
Actual ledger effect of anonymous `/submit` and `/paydbcr` calls (backend host `winmvsb0.hursley.ibm.com` does not resolve from the VM).

Exploitability of the OSV advisories in CBSA-F-02 in this deployment (e.g. Tomcat DIGEST/FORM authenticator CVEs require those authenticators to be configured); severities are as published by OSV/GHSA, not re-scored.
Carbon React front-end (`src/bank-application-frontend`) calls into the Liberty JSON API; its own auth/session handling was out of scope and not reviewed.
